snapshot.title: TNPSC Economy: Rural Welfare & Schemes
snapshot.exam_hook: ⚡ TNPSC Economy Hook: MGNREGA: 2005. NABARD: 1982. Mahalir Thittam: 1989. PURA: Kalam. 100 Days: Work.

quick_notes.title: MGNREGA (2005)
quick_notes.detail: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act. Provides 100 days of guaranteed wage employment. Legal right to work.
quick_notes.explanation: MGNREGA stands for the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, which was passed in 2005. This law gives every adult who lives in a rural area a legal right to ask for work, meaning the government must provide them with a job if they want one. The act guarantees that each rural household will get up to 100 days of paid work in a financial year, usually doing tasks like building roads or cleaning canals. If the government does not give you work within 15 days of you asking for it, they must pay you a daily unemployment allowance instead. This is a legal right, so you can take the government to court if they refuse to give you work or the allowance. The purpose of this law is to reduce poverty in villages by making sure every family has a source of income through manual labor.

quick_notes.title: Self Help Groups (SHGs)
quick_notes.detail: TN is a pioneer in SHGs. "Mahalir Thittam" (1989). Linked with NABARD (est. 1982) for micro-credit.
quick_notes.explanation: Self Help Groups, or SHGs, are small, voluntary groups of about 10 to 20 women from poor households who save small amounts of money regularly and lend that money among themselves. Tamil Nadu, or TN, was a pioneer in this movement, launching a state government program called "Mahalir Thittam" in 1989, which means "Women's Scheme" in Tamil. These SHGs are linked with NABARD, which stands for the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development, an organization established in 1982 to provide rural credit. Through this link, SHGs can access micro-credit, which means very small loans given to poor people who cannot get loans from regular banks, helping them start small businesses or meet urgent needs. The members meet weekly or monthly to collect savings, decide on loans, and repay them, building financial independence and community support. This system empowers women by giving them control over money and decision-making in their households and villages.

quick_notes.title: Housing Schemes
quick_notes.detail: PMAY (Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana) - "Housing for All". IAY (Indira Awas Yojana) was the precursor.
quick_notes.explanation: PMAY stands for Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana, which is a government scheme that aims to provide affordable housing to all eligible citizens, often called "Housing for All". Before this scheme, there was the Indira Awas Yojana, or IAY, which was a similar program focused on helping poor families in rural areas build houses. The PMAY replaced the IAY in 2015 to expand the reach and improve the process for giving housing assistance. Under PMAY, there are separate parts for urban and rural areas, but the overall goal is to make sure every poor family can have a safe and permanent home.

quick_notes.title: Connectivity & Infrastructure
quick_notes.detail: PMGSY (Gram Sadak Yojana) for all-weather roads. PURA (Providing Urban Amenities in Rural Areas - APJ Abdul Kalam).
quick_notes.explanation: Connectivity and Infrastructure means building roads, internet, and other systems so people can travel and communicate easily. The Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana, or PMGSY, is a government program that builds all-weather roads, which are roads that can be used in rain or sun, to connect every village in India to the main road network. The Providing Urban Amenities in Rural Areas, or PURA, is a plan proposed by former President Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam to give villages facilities like electricity, water, and internet, which are normally found in cities. PMGSY focuses only on roads, while PURA covers many different services to make rural life more like urban life. Both programs aim to improve the daily lives of people living in villages by making it easier to travel, work, and access services.

quick_notes.title: Poverty Alleviation
quick_notes.detail: Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) - Food security for poorest of poor. IRDP, TRYSEM, DWACRA merged into SGSY (1999).
quick_notes.explanation: Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) is a government scheme that provides food security, meaning regular, subsidized food grains, to the poorest families who have almost no income. Earlier, three separate programs helped the rural poor: the Integrated Rural Development Program (IRDP) gave assets like livestock or tools to poor families, the Training of Rural Youth for Self Employment (TRYSEM) taught job skills to young people, and the Development of Women and Children in Rural Areas (DWACRA) formed self-help groups for women. In 1999, these three programs were merged into one new scheme called the Swarnajayanti Gram Swaroz
